key_insight: SymAnt combines neural prediction with adaptable symbolic priors to anticipate long sequences of human actions from brief observations. Its core idea is to pair learned patterns with structured reasoning rather than rely on neural predictions alone.
problem_solved: Robots and intelligent systems need to forecast many future actions from limited observations, while purely neural approaches can require extensive context and be difficult to interpret or adjust.
method: Introduce a neuro-symbolic framework for long-horizon action anticipation.
Combine neural networks with structured symbolic priors to ground future-action predictions.
Use adaptable priors to support more interpretable and adjustable anticipation; implementation details are not available in the truncated abstract.
impact: The approach could help practitioners build human-aware systems whose predictions are easier to inspect and adapt. The supplied abstract does not include results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Timeline showing a brief observed action sequence followed by a longer predicted sequence.
Two-branch diagram merging neural predictions and symbolic priors into an action forecast.
Symbolic relationship graph illustrating structured knowledge about actions and context.
Editable-rule icon highlighting adaptable priors and interpretable reasoning.
paper_title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors
paper_authors: Fnu Aryan, Yaqi Xie, Joseph Campbell, Woojun Kim, Kwonjoon Lee
